proposals.hypothesis: LiF is a very wide-gap, electrochemically robust, insulating Li salt. It is thermodynamically resistant to oxidation at 4 V and is less likely than a phosphate to be oxidized by LiCoO2, and it avoids the P/S/O redox products that gave Li3PO4 a large penalty against the sulfide. Its fluoride chemistry is expected to form few reactive products with Li6PS5Cl.
proposals.motivation: Li3PO4 (mp-aaaaaegs) was insulating with a wide gap but had a contact penalty of 0.337 eV/non-Li atom, from reaction with the sulfide to form P2O5, SCl4 and SO2. A different, more inert anion chemistry is needed, so this explores the halide family.

proposals.hypothesis: Li2MgCl4 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating chloride. Its anion matches the Cl in Li6PS5Cl, which should limit anion-exchange reactions at the interface. Mg2+ is hard to reduce, so it should be less prone than Zn or transition metals to forming metal sulfides. Chlorides are also more oxidatively robust than the P/S/B-containing anions that gave the earlier penalties.
proposals.motivation: Li3PO4, LiF and Li3BO3 were all insulating with wide gaps but gave contact penalties of 0.31-0.72 eV/non-Li atom, mostly from reactions that formed P2O5, SCl4, SO2 and borate products. A chloride-based coating is a different family that should avoid those products.

Its O2- framework should be oxidatively robust near 4 V against LiCoO2, and it should avoid the P/S/Cl redox and anion-exchange products that drove the penalties for Li3PO4, LiF, Li3BO3 and Li2MgCl4.
proposal.motivation: Li2O (mp-aaaaacxk) gave the lowest penalty so far (0.189, bin 9), and Li8SiO6 (a Li-rich, fully reduced oxide) also gave a comparatively low value at the oxide end of the set. Li8ZrO6 keeps the Li-rich oxide chemistry but swaps in a more reduction-resistant, Zr4+ framework cation.

proposal.hypothesis: Li5Al(SiO4)2 is a Li-rich, insulating oxide. Al3+ and Si4+ are hard to reduce, so the framework should resist reduction by the sulfide. Its high Li content and O2- framework should keep it close to the Li2O-type behavior that gave the lowest penalty so far, while avoiding the P/S/Cl redox products seen with Li3PO4, LiF and Li2MgCl4.
proposal.motivation: Li2O (mp-aaaaacxk) gave the lowest penalty so far (0.189, bin 9). Li8SiO6 showed that a Li-rich silicate can stay in the oxide regime, but its high penalty came from borate and S/Cl products. Li5Al(SiO4)2 keeps the Li-rich oxide character with a non-reducible Al3+ framework.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3AlSiO5 is a Li-rich mixed Al/Si oxide. Al3+ and Si4+ are hard to reduce, so the framework should resist reduction by the sulfide. Its O2- framework should be oxidatively stable near 4 V against LiCoO2. It is closely related to Li5Al(SiO4)2, which showed zero self-decomposition and no P/S/B redox products, and it is more Li-rich than the Li-poor silicates, which should keep its behavior close to Li2O.
proposal.motivation: Li2O (mp-aaaaacxk) gave the lowest penalty so far (0.189, bin 9). Li5Al(SiO4)2 (mp-aaacroks) had zero self-decomposition and a penalty of 0.31, and it showed that Al/Si-oxide frameworks avoid the P/S/Cl products. Li3AlSiO5 tests a nearby Li-rich Al/Si oxide to see whether the contact penalty can be lowered.

proposal.hypothesis: Li6Ti2O7 is a Li-rich, fully lithiated oxide, which is the chemistry of the best candidate so far (Li2O, penalty 0.189). Its O2- framework should be oxidatively stable near 4 V against LiCoO2. Ti4+ is only moderately reducible, so it should resist the sulfide better than P5+ or B-containing anions, which formed the P2O5, SCl4, SO2 and borate products seen with the other candidates.
proposal.motivation: Li2O (mp-aaaaacxk) gave the lowest penalty so far (0.189, bin 9). Li3PO4, LiF, Li3BO3, Li2MgCl4 and Li8SiO6 all formed P/S/Cl or borate redox and exchange products with larger penalties. A Li-rich oxide with a different framework cation tests whether the Li2O-type low penalty holds for a mixed oxide.
